JUL 1 Mr. Alfonso L. Delgado No. 3 Amaez Street, Btgy. 3, Victonas City. Negros Occidental alphonsedelgado@gmail.com Dear Mr. Delgado. This refers to your Letter dated April 25, 2025 requesting this Department's legal opinion regarding Ordinance No. 2023-591, otherwise known as the "Car-Free Ordinance," enacted on August 30, 2023 by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Victorias. Negros Occidental. The salient facts and circumstances, as culled from your letter, are as follows: The Sangguniang Panlungsod of Victorias City enacted the said ordinance closing Montinola Street, Yap Quifia Street, and Jover Street every first Monday of the month thereby shutting off vehicular access to the City Hall parking lot and diverting all vehicles to Jover Street, Miraflores Street, and Arnaez Streets in Barangay 3. According to you, during the "Car-Free Day," city government vehicles, those vehicles owned by city employees and private individuals, were parked indiscriminately along Arnaez Street and a motorcycle blocking your pedestrian gate.2 The closures and barricades obstruct most direct routes for ambulances, fire trucks, rescue vehicles, and other motor vehicles to the City Health Department, which is located along Montinola Street, to the Immaculate Conception Health Center in Barangay 7, to the Police Station and Bureau of Fire Protection, thereby hinders ease of access to emergency and medical care services. Further, the residents of Barangay 3, specifically, those living in the inner streets of closed Jover, Miraflores, and Arnaez Streets, were not consulted or informed about the subject ordinance prior to its enactment nor review or report was made available to assess the effectiveness of the same. Posed before this Department are your queries which we herein summarized for point of clarity, viz: I. Did the subject ordinance exceed the City's exercise of police power by unduly endangering the pilblic thus contravening its mandate to maintain public safety and public order as well as the immediate access to health care and emergency response services? An Ordinance Declaring Every First Monday of the Month as "Car-Free-l)ay" in the City of Victorias, Negros Occidental 2 Attached photographs showing parked vehicles of the Oilicc of the city Administrator and the Office of the Mayor overcrowding a particular street and a motorcycle blocking a pedestrian gate. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

2. Did the City fail to comply with tho procedures for passing an ordinance affecting property and mobility rights 01 its rosidonts thus violating procedural due process and is unconstitutional? 3. Are there legal temedios availablo [or tho aggriovod party(ios) to sook redress or to challenge tho validity subjoct ordinanco? At the outset, we would like to inform you that this Department is bound by DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-023 dated 17 September 2010 which provides that this Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: (I) xxx (2) Those presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; x x x. For your Query No. I and Query No. 2, we respectfully inform you that this Department is bereft of authority to rule on the legality and validity of Ordinance 2023- 59. In DILG Legal Opinion No. I I I, series 2024, we underscored that "this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare any ordinance or resolution approved by local government officials invalid, nor does it have authority to declare invalid or illegal acts committed by local government officials which is alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code (LGC) or any other applicable laws. The same must be threshed out before the proper forum." By the same token, ordinances are accorded presumption of validity, unless declared invalid by the proper tribunal, because the legislature is presumed to abide by the Constitution.4 In local affairs, the wisdom of local officials must prevail as long as they are acting within the parameters of the Constitution and the law.5 Also, the manner in whi9h ordinances are enacted by the LGUs depends on the internal rules of procedure of the Sanggunian. Consistent with the national policy to devolve powers of the national government and empower political subdivisions, the LGC grants the Sanggunian the authority to adopt its own parliamentary procedure and legislative process.6 Accordingly, in DILG Opinion No. 84, series of 2021, the Department iterated that it is not within its purview to interfere in matters that are internal to the proceedings of the Sanggunian — a local législative body. To do so would risk encroaching upon the constitutionally enshrined principle of local autonomy of LGUs. In this regard, Ordinance No. 2023-59 is presumed legally valid and must be enforced and followed. Until after the judiciary, in an appropriate case, declare its invalidity, it is entitled to obedience and respect.7 Supplement to Memorandum Order No. 2010-01 dated 'l March 2010. For your Query No. 3, the answer is in the affirmative. Any issues concerning the legality or validity of an ordinance may be initiated through a petition for certiorari and prohibition before the proper court in accordance with Rule 65, Sections I and 2 of the Revised Rules of Court, which provides: Section 1. Petition for certiorari. — When any tribunal, board or officer exercising judicial or quasi-judicial functions has acted without or in excess of its or his jurisdiction, or with grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction, and there is no appeal, or any plain, speedy, and adequate remedy in the ordinary course of law, a person aggrieved thereby may file a verified petition in the proper court, alleging the facts with certainty and praying that judgment be rendered annulling or modifying the proceedings of such tribunal, board or officer, and granting such incidental reliefs as law and justice may require. xxx Section 2. Petition for prohibition. — When the proceedings of any tribunal, corporation, board, officer or person, whether exercising judicial, quasi- judicial or ministerial functions, are without or in excess of its or his jurisdiction, or with grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction, and there is no appeal or any other plain, speedy, and adequate remedy in the ordinary course of law, a person aggrieved thereby may file a verified petition in the proper court, alleging the facts with certainty and praying that judgment be rendered commanding the respondent to desist from further proceedings in the action or matter specified therein, or otherwise granting such incidental reliefs as law and justice may require. x x x Thus, this Department opines that the proper remedy to address your grievance against the subject ordinance is to file a verified petition for certiorari and/or prohibition before a court of competént jurisdiction. We again emphasize that the proper courts, and not the DILG, have the legal and binding authority to determine whether an ordinance is invalid or enacted in violation of procedural due process. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: 12-ß—s ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/pau Page 3 of3
